title: A man in Boston won $1 million in the lottery. Then ICE arrested him | CNN
text:
Source: CNN

Over the weekend, the Massachusetts Lotteryshared a pictureof Ariel Velasquez-Morales smiling gently as he gripped an oversized check for $1 million in winnings. On social media, commenters congratulated him, with one person writing they hoped he would be able to “make any dreams come true.”

But Velasquez-Morales was arrested Tuesday by Immigration and Customs Enforcement in East Boston, the same neighborhood where he bought the $10 winning scratch-off ticket from a local market.

He now faces deportation as ICE says the Salvadoran national has been in the country illegally for more than a decade.

“Looks like his luck ran out,” said ICE Assistant Director of Public Affairs Micah Bock in a release announcing the arrest.

It is unclear whether the publication of his lottery winnings attracted ICE’s attention. ICE declined to answer questions from CNN about what led to the arrest or where Velasquez-Morales is being detained.

Velasquez-Morales illegally entered the United States in 2013, during the Obama administration, in the Rio Grande Valley in Texas. Border Patrol agents issued him a notice to appear before an immigration judge, and he was released into the country with a list of free legal service providers, the agency said.

“A Department of Justice immigration judge ordered Velasquez-Morales removed in 2014, but he illegally remained in the country,” the ICE release said.

He will remain in ICE custody pending his removal from the US. CNN has been unable to determine whether he has legal representation.

President Donald Trump has overseen a massive immigration crackdown after promising to lead the largest deportation operation in US history. In his second term, arrests haveshifted away from the borderand focused more on the interior of the country, whereaggressive tacticshave become a hallmark of ICE’s ramped-up detention efforts. By July 2026, there were nearly 66,000 detainees in ICE custody, an increase of nearly 70% from the total detained when Trump took office the year prior.

But after a Republican wipeout in the midterms, Trumphas publicly questionedwhether the tactics were too hard-line and unpopular. It remains to be seen, though, whether he is considering significant changes to his immigration policies.

“Criminal illegal aliens are not welcome in the United States and will be removed as quickly as possible,” ICE said in its release on Velasquez-Morales. “Under President Trump and Secretary Mullin’s leadership, ICE is delivering on its mission to enforce our nation’s immigration laws, restore accountability and protect American communities.”

Velasquez-Morales was playing the lottery’s “$2,000,000 50X Cashword,” in which players scratch cards resembling crossword puzzles to try to reveal complete words. It was thefirst puzzlehe had scratched, the lottery said, and he matched 11 words.

He chose to accept his winnings in cash, which would give him a one-time lump sum of $650,000 before taxes, according to ICE. It is not clear what will happen to his winnings.

Massachusetts lotteryparticipantsdo not need to be legal residents of the state to play, but they must be 21 or older and be located in the state at the time they purchase or play.

CNN has sought comment from the Massachusetts State Lottery Commission.
